$comment: OBRA Level 2 data, written against Level 2 Pista Design Refined.pdf (revision 3). Obstacles declare ability TAGS; satisfying classes resolve from tags.json at load time; no obstacle names a class. The design calls this level L2_PISTA; the runtime id stays 'level_2' because PlayerProfile keys on it. NOTE that LEVEL_2.md is the SUPERSEDED provisional design -- it made Fly the level's new ability, and the refined design restricts flight instead. Do not read it as current.
display_name_note: The artist's spelling, and the folder's. The hub plate says PISTA; the design id keeps L2_PISTA because that exact string is compared in game_level.gd.
goal: recover the seven scraps of the Dagat painting, assemble them, and open the way to Dagat

restrictions.$comment: The design's two rules, as EXPLICIT CLASS LISTS checked against model/labels.json at load. Never infer size or flight from a label at runtime. The size rule is checked FIRST so a butterfly -- which both rules catch -- gets the more specific message.

banned_playable_classes.fiction: small enough to be trampled by the crowd or the parade float
banned_playable_classes.$comment: A REFUSAL, not a violation. The design's flowchart routes both rules to the checkpoint handler, but its own UI list asks for feedback saying WHY a drawing was refused, and its own note says to check the size rule first for the more specific message. Sending the player back to a checkpoint for a drawing they were never allowed to make is a punishment; refusing it at submission is a boundary.

flight_ceiling.drawn_at: the bandarita line in each scene
flight_ceiling.$comment: Per scene, not one global number: whatever Y the bandaritas are strung at, the ceiling sits just under it, and the warning band is DRAWN AT THE LINE so the boundary is the art rather than a HUD element. A line that has been cut caps nothing, so cutting an alley's bunting opens THAT alley's sky -- the trade the cut route makes. `lifted_by_flag` names the flag the cut sets; the lift itself is read off each scene's own line, not off the flag. Both alleys have a line now, at the same measured height (Level2.ALLEY_LINE): the flock nests in it and the cut route climbs to it. run_level2_scene_probe measures both.

scrap_economy.$comment: Each alley's flock carries that alley's pieces and nothing else, and every way through an alley ends with all of them on its floor. The way on does not open until the player has picked up every piece lying there, so nothing is carried from one screen to the next. There used to be a timer on the first flock and a count of escapees carried into Alley 2; Kent: nothing escapes, no timer. Rides the checkpoint.

objectives.$comment: THE OBJECTIVE LINE, one per state of the run. level_2.gd decides which state the player is in; these are only the words, kept here so run_level2_audit can hold them to the rule every dialogue line is held to: no line names a drawable class. A key with a '.tags' twin uses the twin once the obstacle's tags have been taught, and says them in the strip's own words. Never 'door', 'bird', 'key', 'stairs' or 'ladder' -- all five are classes.

objectives.dance: Dance for them. Draw on the beat
objectives.unlock: Get into the house with its light on
objectives.unlock.tags: Draw something that can {tags} at the house with its light on
objectives.startle.tags: Draw something that can {tags} beside the dancers
objectives.fetch_light: Go into the house with its light on
objectives.take_light: Take the candle off the table
objectives.to_church: Take the candle to the church
objectives.rack: Put the candle on the rack
objectives.to_alleys: Go out the back of the church, into the alleys
objectives.back_to_church: Go back through the church to the alleys
objectives.flock: Get her scraps back from the flock
objectives.flock.tags: Get her scraps back. Draw something that can {tags}
objectives.flock_feed: Put something out for them to come down to
objectives.flock_feed.tags: Draw something that can {tags}, and set it down for them
objectives.flock_climb: Set something under the strings to climb
objectives.flock_climb.tags: Draw something that can {tags}, and set it under the strings

objectives.flock_cut.tags: Climb up to the strings and {tags} them down
objectives.flock_stone: Draw something to throw at them
objectives.flock_stone.tags: Draw something that can {tags}, to throw at them

objectives.flock_fetch: Pick your stone back up where it landed

artist.$comment: NOT ANSWERED BY DRAWING, which is a first for this project -- so it declares `answered_by` and the audit skips the two-answer floor for it rather than failing a route that was never a tag question. The level stays unloseable: clear it in one or two attempts for the flower, fail both and the kandila is handed over anyway. Only the flower is at stake, and the loss is SILENT by design -- a secret ending that announces its requirements is not secret.

pragmatist.$comment: The lit house past two or three dark doors, so the search reads as a search. Reuses Level 1's lock-imitation mechanic -- shared code, shared lock art. TWO answers, which is the floor; the audit prints it.

protector.$comment: The dancers scatter and NEVER RETURN -- MG_People needs a no-dancers variant for every scene after this. That is the Protector cost here: the plaza is Lolo's memory and the player has just emptied it. Closing the Artist route the moment they scatter must be signalled BEFORE the player commits.

obstacles.$comment: THE SAME THREE WAYS IN BOTH ALLEYS -- Kent: the three choices apply "to the two areas where the player needs to collect the parts of the painting". Five birds here, one piece each. The flock flies the alley and nests in the bunting between flights; whichever way it is answered, every piece ends up on the floor and the player picks them up by walking over them. The way on opens when all five are in hand. Nothing escapes and nothing runs on a clock, so no path can lose a piece. The fork is asked out loud at the alley's entrance, after Lolo has seen the flock.

artist.$comment: Set down where they can see it, and every bird in the alley comes down to it, eats, and leaves its piece beside it. One offering for the whole flock: splitting it per bird would turn a lore beat into a chore. `bucket` is a tool and is used where the player stands, which is where they come down.

pragmatist.choice_note:
NEEDS  CLIMB,  then  CUT
something to get you up to the strings, then an edge to cut them down
pragmatist.$comment: TWO DRAWINGS, the way Kent asked for it: something to get up to the strings, and something to cut them with. The strings come down, the nests with them, and the flock bolts and lets go of every piece. The climb is something the APO stands on -- the cut needs the apo's hands -- so the climbing creatures are out: `spider` is banned here anyway, `bat` is a flight-ceiling class reaching for the ceiling, and a `monkey` or `crab` up a wall has nothing to cut with. `elephant` cuts by being an elephant and cannot get up there. The cutting edge has to be used within reach of the strings (Level2.CUT_REACH), which from the floor it is not. It lifts THIS alley's ceiling -- the flight cap is read off the line in each scene, and a line that is down caps nothing.

protector.choice_note:
NEEDS  STRIKE
something to throw at them — aim it, and let go
protector.$comment: THROWN, and aimed: a dotted arc from the hand shows where it will go (StoneThrow2D). The first half is drawing something to throw -- a round shape is recognised as a circle and becomes a stone; a boomerang or a cannon is thrown the same way from the hand. The second half is every bird knocked down, one throw at a time, and it is answered by the last piece coming down rather than by a drawing. A miss costs nothing but the walk: a stone lies where it landed and is picked back up, a boomerang comes back, a cannon keeps its shot. THE EXCLUSIONS ARE ABOUT WHAT LEAVES THE HAND: a blade swings inside UtilityObject.TOOL_REACH and the anvil drops straight down, and StoneThrow2D.THROWN names what can be thrown. `requires_reach_px` is how high above the alley floor the route has to be able to hit -- the strings, where the nests are -- and run_level2_audit measures every answer's real throw against it.

hidden_flowers_note: Level 2 has NO hidden flower. Its one collectible is the dance minigame's, awarded at L2_N1's Artist route and recorded through PlayerProfile.record_collectible so EndingResolver counts it like every other. Level 1's cross_level_effect used to name a hidden_flower_2 here; see the crease note below.

canvas_2_creased.does: draws the fold through the plaza it creased -- canvas_2_pista IS this plaza -- and has Lolo say so as the level opens
canvas_2_creased.does_not: change the scrap count, the paths available, or the ending
canvas_2_creased.$comment: VISUAL ONLY. See LEVEL_1.md and LEVEL_TEMPLATE.md: this is a recorded debt, not a design -- Level 1's Node 3 Protector now costs nothing mechanical.

made_a_key_in_level_1.does: varies L2_N1's Pragmatist dialogue -- Lolo says they have done this before

cultural_constraints.$comment: The plaza is a church plaza and the fiesta is a religious feast. Level 1 asserted its guardrails in code rather than only documenting them; this level owes the same.

church.altar_reachable_for: placing the kandila, and nothing else
church.note: The bulul rule ported. No cutting, burning, breaking or standing on any sacred image -- the cross on the pediment, the retablo, a carroza if one is ever drawn. ⚠ AND THE SANTO NINO ESPECIALLY: it is the most venerated image in the country, it appears in the Basilica's facade niche and in the retablo indoors, and in both places it is DRAWN INTO A TEXTURE and owns no node, no area and no collision. ChurchInterior2D._check_the_guardrail fails loudly if anybody gives it one.

audio.note: Inverts Level 1's list: Payyo forbids bandurria because it is not Cordilleran; in a Cebu plaza the rondalla, the town brass band and the Sinulog drum-and-bugle are exactly right. A real Mass looped as ambience is not ambience, and neither is a recording of the novena.

cultural_constraints.fiesta_is_named: Santo Nino -- the Basilica Minore del Santo Nino, Cebu, and Sinulog (third Sunday of January)
cultural_constraints.fiesta_naming_note: CHANGED 2026-09-01, deliberately, and this is the record of it. This level was Pahiyas: Lucban, Quezon, San Isidro Labrador, 15 May -- because the delivered plaza painting is unmistakably that fiesta, a woven-palm arch crowned with a kiping aranya. The plaza is now authored art themed on the Basilica del Santo Nino instead (coral stone in three tiers, the belfry beside it, bahay na bato along the street, Sinulog's red and gold), so the config follows the level rather than the other way round. The delivered painting is still in the repo and still backs the hub card. Half-committing is the failure mode: this is Cebu now, not Lucban.

arch_is_food.note: KEPT AS A RULE EVEN THOUGH THE ARCH IS GONE. The kiping arch belonged to Pahiyas and went with the re-theme, so nothing in the level touches it because nothing in the level has one. The rule stays because the reasoning does: kiping IS the harvest, the way Level 1's straw pile is grain, and if a palm arch is ever drawn again it is food and not scenery to be cut up.

load_time_assertions: every obstacle route resolves >= 2 classes AFTER exclusions
every obstacle route resolves >= 2 classes AFTER exclusions AND after the banned-class list is subtracted
every class named in restrictions.banned_playable_classes and restrictions.flight_ceiling exists in model/labels.json
no route both requires a flight-ceiling class and asks the player to cross the ceiling
every tag in tags_unlocked exists in entities.json
every morph-capable route is preceded by a checkpoint
every teaches_before_choice tag is unlocked before its choice is presented
a route answered by something other than drawing declares answered_by
no dialogue line in this level names a class
all seven scraps are recoverable on every path combination
